title: Beyond Proxy Metrics: MLLMs as Human Surrogates for Explainable AI Evaluation
claim: Evaluation can be organized by purpose-grounded areas with clear metrics, then automated by simulating user studies with a surrogate model.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right; applications map to purpose areas, then to a simulation
description: The figure has three columns, read left to right. The left column, titled 'What is the Application?', is a stack of orange boxes listing example applications such as LLM alignment debugging, Alzheimer's biomarker discovery, loan recourse and movie recommendation. Ellipses separate the boxes. Curved arrows link them to the middle column, 'Identify Purpose-Grounded Area and Metric'. That column has five cartoon illustrations of a robot and a human, each with a bold area name (Model Improvement, Knowledge-Extraction, Reliance Calibration, Actionable Recommendation, System Engagement). Under each name is a pink box with a metric question and a label M_mi, M_ke, M_rc, M_ar or M_se. Blue lines merge these labels into a single arrow pointing at the right column, 'Simulate User Study With MLLM'. That column shows a brain-and-magnifier icon, a description of the simulated user study, a ranking ξ1 ≽ ξ2 ≽ … ≽ ξn, and a final box reading 'Identify best explainability method for application.'
caption: Purpose-grounded evaluation framework. Our framework for how XAI evaluation can be complemented using MLLMs as surrogate human users. We structure this evaluation around purpose-grounded domains in the literature because they contain clear evaluation metrics and are the areas XAI has proven most useful, here we show five of those. With both the purpose and metric to hand, researchers can simulate appropriate user testing to help identify if their method is more promising than current baselines or not. Importantly, note this framework can (and should) also be used with real humans in place of the MLLM, as we illustrate during this paper's experiments in Sections [ref]-[ref].
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) has expanded into a broad and impactful research area, but the fundamental question of how best to evaluate explanation techniques has proven frustratingly elusive. Methodologies typically revolve around either proxy metrics which tell us little about the utility of an explanation, or human evaluation which---while generally considered the gold standard---is expensive, difficult to scale, and challenging to reproduce. In this paper, we investigate if Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can act as surrogate human participants to automate the evaluation of XAI. To do this, we first propose a ``purpose-grounded'' evaluation framework with metrics applicable to both MLLMs and human users alike. Then, we offer some conceptual insights as to why and when we can trust these models to automate this process. Lastly, we conduct extensive empirical testing across five purpose-grounded areas such as model improvement and fourteen popular MLLMs. Results indicate that all models trend positively, but OpenAI and Qwen models generally show higher alignment compared to other variants, which would be the recommended choices in practice. We expect our insights not to replace user testing, but rather to help XAI researchers complement their current evaluation methodologies and move the field away from heavy reliance on proxy metrics for measuring explanation utility.
